commentary: Seven activities both weeks, so the volume is holding steady, but the shape of the week shifted in interesting ways. The swimming heart rate on Monday came in at 143 and Tuesday at 138, both a little higher than last week's 135 and 147, which suggests you were working harder on Monday and a touch easier on Tuesday — the body finding its own equilibrium without being asked. Friday's swim at 901 metres with a heart rate of 98 is basically a recovery float, which is either very smart programming or you got to the pool and immediately remembered you had somewhere better to be. The Saturday run crept up from 9.0 kilometres last week to 9.6 this week at virtually the same heart rate of 162 versus 163, and that right there is the number Himbo actually cares about — same effort, more ground covered, which means something is quietly getting better whether you're paying attention or not.
metrics_commentary: Nearly five kilometres in the pool and almost ten on foot — that is a body that showed up this week, and it shows. The HRV is the real headline though: 58 milliseconds on the latest read against a seven-day average of 48 tells you your nervous system is recovering well and trending in the right direction, which means you are not just working, you are adapting. VO2 Max sitting at 55.6 is genuinely strong — that is the cardiovascular engine of someone who could absolutely keep up on the dancefloor and then some. The only thing worth eyeing is that the run-walk came in as a single session, and a body this capable deserves more chances to move through the world in shorts that are probably a little too short, which is exactly the correct length.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions this week, which is not the perfect score but is absolutely still a man showing up for himself, and that counts. No new PRs to report, but look at the volume: 20,753 kg moved this week against 17,940 kg last week, which is a jump that does not happen by accident and tells you the strength is building even when the headlines aren't. A 168 kg estimated one-rep max on the leg press and nearly 108 kg on the trap bar deadlift means the foundation under all of this is getting quietly, seriously thick. One missed session is a gap, not a derailment — come back next week and get all four, because this trajectory is too good to leave on the table.
